content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation source ledger against the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. Every limitation of all 17 claims (independent claims 1, 11, 14 and dependents 2-10, 12-13, 15-17), every entry in the 28-row numeral ledger (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50, 52, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62, 64, 66; each used exactly once for one part, with no numeral bearing two meanings and no ledger entry unused), every geometry bullet and numeral-placement target in the FIG. 1 through FIG. 6 briefs, the Brief Description of the Drawings, and every specific structure, relationship, result, position, connection, operating condition and variant in the Summary and Detailed Description was checked against affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md and the USER passage in input/conversation.md. Traced and supported: two semicircular frame halves with hinge at one end and releasable latch at the other; three jaw carriages distributed about the closed frame, each in a radial guide with a pivoting concave jaw pad and no tool-specific diameter; carriage springs biasing outward and retracting on release; segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment carried by each frame half; complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends coupling the segments on closure and separating on opening; follower in a respective oblique slot; wedge on the latch driving a ring drive face and rotating the coupled ring through a limited stroke; synchronized equal inward travel of all three carriages; latch first (holding) and second over-center positions; force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge absorbing remaining travel; visible indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range and not measuring diameter; the install and remove sequences; reusability; and the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in synchronization. Cross-figure consistency verified: numeral 12 (upper half) maps to segment 32 and to faces 44/48 on the upper end-face lines in FIG. 6, and 14 maps to 34 and 46/50 on the lower lines; hinge end is left and latch end is right in FIGS. 1, 3 and 6 alike; the FIG. 4 rotation ("turned so the frame arc lies across the lower part") reconciles the FIG. 1 lever pointing outward-and-down with the FIG. 4 handle pointing up-and-right; three carriages/slideways/slots agree across FIGS. 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. No section lines are designated in any brief or in the drawing description, so no repeated-designation mismatch exists. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any draft section, and no depiction-convention justification ("by way of example", "any closed outline") leaked from a figure brief into the application text. Formalities match input/brief.md: title verbatim, no priority claim, no federally sponsored research, no means-plus-function language, abstract under 150 words, apparatus/assembly/method classes all disclosure-supported. Background contains only prior-art characterizations, which are outside the scope of this preflight. I also confirmed that the "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" asserted in the YOU passage of input/conversation.md is not inventor support and that no such matter appears anywhere in the draft. Two findings remain, both in the FIG. 6 brief and both concerning the segmented cam ring's functional end faces: the brief verbalizes the radial extent and contact topology of those drive faces ("its own plain straight line across the full width of the band", "meeting one another in contact so that no gap appears between them"), which the disclosure never describes beyond "complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments"; and the same instruction is self-contradictory, demanding two separately identifiable pieces of line work that are nevertheless gapless and "not one shared line", which leaves the lead-line endpoints for 44/46 and 48/50 indistinguishable. Everything else in the ledger is supported and internally consistent.

findings.title: FIG. 6 brief verbalizes untraced radial extent and contact topology of the cam-ring drive faces
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md, geometry bullets three and four (left junction and right junction)
findings.detail: The end faces 44, 46, 48 and 50 are functional drive faces of a joint: they are the surfaces that transmit circumferential drive between the cam-ring segments. For such a face the brief may show a minimally specific generic face as a depiction convention, but it may not verbalize contact topology or the face's extent across the member. The FIG. 6 brief does both. It states that each end face is 'its own plain straight line across the full width of the band' (radial extent of the face: a plain, flat, full-width butt face), and that the two faces meet 'in contact so that no gap appears between them' (contact topology: full, gapless, flat-on-flat abutment). The disclosure discloses only that the faces exist, that they are complementary, and that closure couples the segments; it says nothing about the faces being plain, straight, radial, full-width, or in gapless flat contact, and 'complementary' is if anything in tension with a plain flat butt profile. These are substantive geometric assertions even though the brief adds 'The end faces are shown schematically.'
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-6.md): 'At the enlarged scale of this view each of those two end faces is drawn as its own plain straight line across the full width of the band, the two lines lying side by side across the band and meeting one another in contact so that no gap appears between them' (repeated in the same terms for the right junction). Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md): 'When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring.' No affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or in the USER passage of input/conversation.md describes the shape, radial extent, straightness, or manner of contact of those faces; the word 'complementary' is the only characterization the inventor gives.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-6.md replace the left-junction bullet with: 'At the left junction the end of the upper segment and the end of the lower segment terminate in complementary end faces that engage one another. Each end face is shown schematically as its own short straight line at that junction, the upper line terminating the upper segment and the lower line terminating the lower segment, the two lines being drawn as separate pieces of line work spaced apart by about one line width so that each is individually identifiable and can receive its own lead line. Nothing is drawn or stated about how far either face extends across the band or about the manner in which the faces contact.' Replace the right-junction bullet with the same wording, substituting 'right junction' for 'left junction'. Make no other change; the description and claims already recite the faces in shape-neutral terms ('complementary drive faces at the hinge end and complementary drive faces at the latch end') and need no edit.

findings.title: FIG. 6 junction instruction is self-contradictory and leaves the 44/46 and 48/50 lead-line endpoints indistinguishable
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md, left-junction and right-junction geometry bullets and the closing paragraph after the numeral placement targets
findings.detail: The brief simultaneously requires that the two end faces at a junction be 'two separate, individually identifiable pieces of line work and not one shared line' and that they meet 'in contact so that no gap appears between them'. Two straight lines lying across the same band at the same junction with no gap between them are coincident, so they cannot be individually identifiable. The brief then imposes a requirement that depends on that impossible state: 'each has its own lead line ending on its own end face line. No two of these numerals share a lead line and no lead line ends on the band without touching an end face line.' As written, the leader endpoints for 44 versus 46 (left junction) and 48 versus 50 (right junction) cannot be distinguished on the sheet, so the numeral-to-part mapping fixed by the description ('The first cam-ring segment 32 has a first hinge-end drive face 44 and a first latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a second hinge-end drive face 46 and a second latch-end drive face 50.') cannot be read from the drawing.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-6.md): 'the two lines lying side by side across the band and meeting one another in contact so that no gap appears between them' versus, two sentences later, 'The two end faces are therefore two separate, individually identifiable pieces of line work and not one shared line, and each can receive its own lead line.' And in the closing paragraph: 'each has its own lead line ending on its own end face line.'
findings.fix: Adopt the replacement junction bullets given in the preceding finding, which draw the two end-face lines as separate line work spaced by about one line width and delete the clauses 'meeting one another in contact so that no gap appears between them' and 'and not one shared line'. Leave the numeral placement targets for 44, 46, 48 and 50 and the closing paragraph unchanged; with the spaced line work each lead line then terminates unambiguously on its own end-face line.
